title: Sonny and the Big Old Gum Tree | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka finds the oldest, biggest gum tree in the whole bush and leans against it, feeling all the hundreds of years of patience and rootedness moving through the bark into her. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The tree was old.

Sunny knew it the moment she saw it — not because it was particularly taller than the other gums, but because of how it held itself. Wide. Patient. Completely settled in its place. Its bark was rough and ribboned, peeling in long grey-white strips. Its trunk was so wide she couldn't have reached her arms around even a quarter of it.

She put her paw flat against the bark.

The tree was still warm from the day — or perhaps that was something else. Something older. She pressed harder.

She thought: this tree was here before I was born. Before my mother was born. Before her mother. Before anyone she could name. It has just been here, growing slowly, year by year, holding its place.

She walked around the base slowly.

The roots were enormous — great arching wooden cables that surfaced above the ground and dove back in. Between them were hollows where other things lived. She could hear something small breathing in one of them.

She sat down in the curve of a root.

The root was smooth and warm.

She leaned her back against the trunk.

She felt the tree behind her — solid, patient, permanent. Still growing. Always growing.

She thought: nothing is wrong when you have your back to something this old.

And she slept, held by a tree that had been waiting for exactly this.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, big old tree. Goodnight, little one.
